message.content: Lead: 35 → 7 and net −159K boxes: good. One last pattern, the same one the other lanes used: each law should read NOTHING in an item that can't hold its shape. Gate `withins_refused` on the item having a `within` at all, `uses_in`/`reexports_in`/`cycles_closed` on the item having an `export use`, and `enum_traits_untraited` on the item declaring a `collect enum`, each through a cheap per-item fact already in the item's facts (a kind or flag, no walk). <to_controller>dev-tools bundle not sent: the cost slice is red on 403f8527 and mine. Gates are otherwise green, 22/23 (avrac-a's 2 stale-citation rows are land58's). In the cost slice, `check --counts packages/cli` was killed at 8258 MB (cap 8000 MB). land58 on the same machine runs every workload under the cap; its own 32 "new candidate" rows against the snap57 baseline are land58's, not mine. Suspects: two of my laws walk package-wide state per item or line, uncached. collect_enum_member_implements rescans every package `collect enum` for each item, and reexport_acyclic re-walks package reach for each `export use` line. Both are now package-level queries (`package_owed_gatherings`, `package_uses_reached`). A peak-RSS comparison of plain cold `check packages/cli` (land58 vs 403f8527) is running; then the fix's measurement, then cost again.</to_controller>

The dev-tools bundle is held: the cost slice is red on my head, and the cause is my change, not land58.

**What failed:** the cost slice's cold `check --counts packages/cli` was killed at 8,258 MB, over its 8,000 MB memory cap. land58 on this machine finishes every cost workload under the cap. It fails the slice for a different reason: 32 new candidate rows against an older baseline, which come with land58. All the other gates pass on 403f8527, apart from avrac-a's two stale-citation rows, which you confirmed are land58's.

**Likely cause:** two of my new laws do package-wide work over and over without caching it, which gets very expensive on the cli check because it covers every std package:
- `collect_enum_member_implements` rescans every `collect enum` in the package once per item.
- `reexport_acyclic` re-walks which packages reach which for every `export use` line.

**Fix (written, not yet built):** each walk is now a query computed once per package, `package_owed_gatherings` and `package_uses_reached`. The laws' behaviour is unchanged.

**Now:** a plain cold `check packages/cli` is running with land58's compiler and then mine, recording peak memory for each. I'm holding the rebuild until it finishes so the two can't compete for memory. Then I build the fix, measure it, re-run the cost slice, and send the bundle only once no row is over tolerance.

#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
# A SHALLOW CLONE FETCHES THE ONE COMMIT IT PINS.
# The cold workloads: a name, the machine's store it runs over, the census tables it takes, then the
# command the census compiler runs in the snapshot. A STORE IS NOT THE COMPILER: every run but one has
# the machine's store off, so its rows are what the compiler does, whatever a store holds;
# `cold-with-store-fill` is the cli's cold check over an empty store, which it fills — the store's own
# price, ratcheted apart, its sites the check's own and so read once, from check-cli. The death
# census stamps a word per 16 bytes of slab, half again the memory a run holds, so the build — the
# largest run, its fns the check's own — takes the site tables alone, under the cap.

a moved shape would hand every annotation the wrong values. The program
layer had no such door, ran the annotation over the moved package and said
its verdict (annotation.said), so the registry's witness fired on the old
path alone.

One question for both paths: `meta_moved_from` (features/crossing) takes
the loaded records' slots and `Node`'s variants and answers the first that
moved; the old path's `meta_disagreement` asks it of its decls, the layer's

one non-absent scalar field rides inline, as the runtime lays it out —
`Spelled.mark`). `meta_door` says it in the old path's words
(`meta_foreign`, now both paths' voice), past the manifests' door — on
stdout from `build`, `check` and `run`, and first in a held program's
judgement.

before, the old path's refusal on both after. The real `@std/meta` moves

collect_enum.trait on the program layer: a trait word naming no trait, a member without its impl

The old path refuses a `collect enum E: T` two ways: `T` names a
declaration that is no trait (at the word), and a gathered member writes no
impl of `T`, where `T` derives none (at the member's declaration). The
program layer had no law of the kind, so the registry's witness fired on the
old path alone. Two laws, in the old path's words (`no_trait_said`,
`unimplemented_said`):

- `collect_enum_over_a_trait` reads the enum's trait words: one resolving
  to a declaration other than a trait is refused; one resolving to nothing
  stays resolve's.
- `collect_enum_member_implements` reads each item from the member's side —
  a `collect enum … in package` gathers across files — and refuses a
  declaration a package enum gathers that writes no impl of a trait the enum
  names and that derives none.

Witnesses collect_enum_names_no_trait (the registry's) and
collect_enum_member_unimplemented: silent on the layer before, both paths'
words at the same site after. features/collects tests: 96/105 on land58,
99/105 after — the three `collect enum E: T` cases (960, 1010, 1030) turn
green; the six still failing fail on land58 alike.

content.content:
[package]
name        = "@std/avrac"
version     = "0.0.1"
description = "Avra compiler library"

[lib]
name = "std-avrac"
path = "src/avrac.av"

# THE HOST SEAM's other half: language/llvm_api.av declares the C
# binding's prototypes; these keep the promise at link time. The
# prefix comes from the environment, so no machine's paths live in
# the tree — `LLVM_PREFIX` is what the Makefile passes.
[link]
# ffi.o is the EXTERN HOST's frame — the evaluator's way to call a
# linked C function by name. It is the COMPILER's C and rides here so
# that it never reaches a user's binary: every program the compiler
# emits links the runtime library, and a symbol resolver there would ship
# inside all of them.
objects = ["../../build/llvm_wrapper.o", "../../build/ffi.o"]
# ffi.o resolves the running image's own symbols by name, so a program
# linking this package keeps every symbol in its dynamic table.

#!/bin/sh
# THE PROGRAM LAYER REFUSES WHAT THE OLD PATH REFUSES, CODE BY CODE: every registered code's witness
# (packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/dev/witnesses.av, dumped by tools/witness-files) laid out on disk
# as a package, checked on the old path — built, for a witness the old path judges by building —
# and built on the program layer — checked, where the old refusal stands in a test file, which a
# build reads only where its entry reaches it — then judged by the first line each says:
#   SAME            both refuse, in the same first line
#   DIFFERENT       the program layer refuses under the old kind, in other words
#   OTHER-ERROR     the program layer refuses under another kind
#   ACCEPTED        the program layer builds what the old path refuses
#   UNBUILT         the program layer says it doesn't build the program yet, and refuses nothing
#   COMPILER-DEFECT the program layer crashed, ran out its time, or failed saying no refusal
#   OLD-SILENT      the old path refuses nothing over the witness either
#   WARNED / WARN-MISSING   a warning's witness: the program layer says the old warning, or doesn't
#   BEYOND / ABSENT no source reaches the code / no witness is written yet
#   STD-ROOT        the witness lays out a std of its own, which a compiler on disk reads only beside
#                   itself — not run
#   NEW-ONLY        the witness uses a form only the program layer builds (`avra tapes --new-only`):
#                   skipped, never asked of the old path, and counted
# Prints one row per code that isn't SAME (code, verdict, the lane whose kinds it is — a guess from
# the kind — and both first lines), then the counts. With --bar N it exits 1 where fewer than N are
# SAME, else 0.
#   sh tools/witness_program_differential.sh [compiler] [--bar N] [--jobs J] [code…]
#   (default build/avra-try; J defaults to 3; naming codes judges only those)
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
avra=build/avra-try
case "${1:-}" in --*|"") ;; *) avra=$1; shift ;; esac
case $avra in /*) ;; *) avra="$root/$avra" ;; esac
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "witness_program_differential: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
bar=0
jobs=3
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
        --bar) bar=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --jobs) jobs=$2; shift 2 ;;
        *) break ;;
    esac
done
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'find "$tmp" -delete' EXIT
cp -R "$root/tools/witness-files" "$tmp/dump"
find "$tmp/dump" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \;
(cd "$tmp/dump" && AVRA_PROGRAM=0 "$avra" run . >"$tmp/witnesses.jsonl" 2>"$tmp/dump.err") || {
    echo "witness_program_differential: the witnesses could not be dumped:" >&2
    cat "$tmp/dump.err" >&2
    exit 1
}
python3 -I "$root/tools/witness_program_differential.py" "$avra" "$tmp" "$bar" "$jobs" "$@"

The program layer's surface folds each `export use` as parity-resolve-2's
`module_exports` does — what the module it names declares, through
`with_shapes(own_shapes)`, components, grammars and instances alike — and
this lane's own cross-package fold (`module_exports_past`,
`reexported_shapes`) is gone: their verb reaches a module of another
package already, through `imported_module`.

The old path's `line_words` folds a re-export the same way, one level
(`line_words_as`): what the module a re-export names declares, never what
that one re-exports in turn, so it needs no seen-set to end, and it carries
grammars and instances as the layer does, not components alone.

their stray guard on the proof; a live `run --eval` says a refusal on stdout,
as `run` does; a lowered fn keeps both `unbuilt` and `built_once`.

# `flow.no_fate` keyed by marks, not by a field named `dead` — design note

Status: proposal only. Nothing is built. The fate pair (f49a0160 here, a86951ac on my branch) is held out of every bundle.

Disclosure: `const fate_field = "dead"` (old path) and `FATE_FIELD` (layer) were already in the tree before the pair (71e734ea has both). The pair deepened the problem by also reading a *queue's* `dead`. Its fate-raising and help text name `dead:` literally as well. This design removes all of it.

## 1. The marks

Three markers in `@std/meta`, declared like `@unbroken` and `@bracket`. The compiler recognises each one by resolving the annotation to its `@std.meta` declaration (`is_meta_fn`: package plus declared name), never by what the user's field is called:

```avra
/// The field is where the failures of the handler field `_handler`, of the same component, go.
export fn fate_for(_f: Field, _handler: string) {}

/// The field holds a component whose `@fate` field takes the failures of the handler `_handler`:
/// the handler's fate may be borrowed from what this field holds.
export fn fate_from(_f: Field, _handler: string) {}

/// The field is this component's fate: the destination that a component holding this one may
/// borrow through `@fate_from`. It names no handler, because the component holding it brings the
/// handler.
export fn fate(_f: Field) {}
```

Spelling on a component (component fields already take marks: `cfield = ( marks:mark )* …`):

```avra
export component worker<T, R, E> {
    @fate_from(each) reads: queue<T>?
    each: fn(Delivery<T>) -> Result<R, E>
    @fate_for(each) dead: queue<Dead<T, E>>? = null
}
```

The argument `each` is a bare name. It resolves against the component's *own* fields, so the only name involved is the author's own declaration. Precedent (`@bracket("decls")`, `plain_field`) writes it as a string. I'd take whichever the owner prefers; bare is the lead's spelling.

## 2. What the law reads (both paths)

At the declaration, each component field gets a fate seat: `Own` (`@fate`), `For(h)`, `From(h)`, or none.
- Layer: on `FieldSeat` / `RecordShape`, beside the existing `valued`.
- Old path: read off `component_parts_of(d).fields()` marks through `decls.is_meta_annotation`.

An instance of component C owes a fate for handler field `h` only when:
- some field of C is marked `@fate_for(h)` or `@fate_from(h)`; and
- the value written for `h` can fail (a fn answering `Result`).

A component with no marks owes nothing, as one with no `dead` owes nothing today.

The fate is named when **any** of these holds:
- **Direct.** A `@fate_for(h)` field is written non-`null`, or left to a default that is a value (today's `valued` / `defaults_to_value`).
- **Borrowed.** A `@fate_from(h)` field's value traces, through the name (`instance_named` follows the `let` / named instance, as now), to an instance whose `@fate` field is named in the direct sense.
- **Borrowed, untraced.** The value traces to no instance (a parameter, a call's answer). It is taken as named, as now: only a fate known to be missing is refused.

Otherwise the law refuses at `h`'s value, with the same code and message as today. The help names the field **from the mark**, never a constant:
- with only `@fate_for` fields: "name a fate for it — `<field>: …`", where `<field>` is the `@fate_for(h)` field's declared name;
- with a `@fate_from` field: "name the fate on what it reads — `<own field>: …` on `<instance>`", where `<own field>` is the borrowed component's `@fate` field name and `<instance>` is the traced name.

That is the pair's logic unchanged (own first, then queue, then trace through the `let`). Only the key changes: "a field called `dead`" becomes "the field that wears the mark".

## 3. What refuses a mark (new law at the declaration, e.g. `component.fate_mark`; both paths, with witnesses)

1. `@fate_for(h)` or `@fate_from(h)` where `h` names no field of the component: "`h` is no field of `C`".
2. `h` names a field that is not a handler that can fail (not a fn answering `Result`): "a fate is for a handler that can fail; `h` cannot".
3. `@fate_for(h)`, `@fate_from(h)` or `@fate` on a fn-typed field: a handler cannot be a destination.
4. `@fate_from(h)` on a field whose type (with `?` stripped) is not a component declaring a `@fate` field: "`reads` holds a `box`, which marks no `@fate` field to borrow".
5. Two `@fate` fields on one component, or two `@fate_for(h)` fields for the same `h`: ambiguous destination.
6. Any of the three marks outside a component field (a plain record or a fn): refused as misplaced. They mean nothing there.

No field type is required of a direct destination beyond "not a fn". The destination's type is the author's (a `queue<Dead<…>>`, a `Sink`, a `string` name): the compiler doesn't know what a letter is, and that's the point.

## 4. Migration

**std-queue as it stands**
- `worker`: add `@fate_for(each)` on `dead`. That is the only field the law reads today.
- `queue` has **no** `dead` field today, so it has nothing to mark. `@fate_from(each) reads` is added only if and when services move the letter onto the queue: the `queue` then declares `@fate <letter field>`, the `worker` marks `reads`, and the `worker`'s `dead` stays as its own override. Marking `reads` before that refuses under rule 4, deliberately: a borrow from something that has no fate is a mistake.
- `job`: stays unmarked. It always builds its worker with a fate (`buries_in ?? letter_made()`), so it owes nothing at the instance, as today.

**Compiler**
- Delete `fate_field` / `FATE_FIELD`.
- The help strings stop spelling `dead:`, and `fate_unqueued`'s help takes the field names.
- Remedy and witness rows (`remedies.av` around lines 609 and 798, `witnesses.av` around 1453) mark their toy `work` component's `dead`.
- `components_fate_test.av` cases mark their components.
- `tools/program-refusals/fate_*`: the toy `box` gets `@fate dead`, `crew` gets `@fate_from(each) reads` / `@fate_for(each) dead`, and `job` gets `@fate_for(each) dead`. Expectations are unchanged, except that the help names the field from the mark.
- New witnesses: one per refusal in §3, plus a component whose fate field is named something other than `dead` (e.g. `@fate_for(run) graveyard`), to prove nothing keys on the spelling.

**Users.** A user component with a `dead:` field and no mark stops owing a fate. That is a silent loosening, so it needs a note in the release text. Inside the tree the only such components are the toys and std-queue's `worker`, all migrated above.

## Open for the owner
- Bare name or string argument (`@fate_for(each)` vs `@fate_for("each")`).
- Whether `@fate` / `@fate_from` land now (as general machinery, with only the witnesses using them) or with services' move of the letter onto the queue. `@fate_for` alone covers std-queue today.

Status: proposal only. Nothing is built. The fate pair (f49a0160 here, a86951ac on my branch) is held out of every bundle.

Disclosure: `const fate_field = "dead"` (old path) and `FATE_FIELD` (layer) were already in the tree before the pair (71e734ea has both). The pair deepened the problem by also reading a *queue's* `dead`. Its fate-raising and help text name `dead:` literally as well. This design removes all of it.

## 1. The marks

Three markers in `@std/meta`, declared like `@unbroken` and `@bracket`. The compiler recognises each one by resolving the annotation to its `@std.meta` declaration (`is_meta_fn`: package plus declared name), never by what the user's field is called:

```avra
/// The field is where the failures of the handler field `_handler`, of the same component, go.
export fn fate_for(_f: Field, _handler: string) {}

/// The field holds a component whose `@fate` field takes the failures of the handler `_handler`:
/// the handler's fate may be borrowed from what this field holds.
export fn fate_from(_f: Field, _handler: string) {}

/// The field is this component's fate: the destination that a component holding this one may
/// borrow through `@fate_from`. It names no handler, because the component holding it brings the
/// handler.
export fn fate(_f: Field) {}
```

Spelling on a component (component fields already take marks: `cfield = ( marks:mark )* …`):

```avra
export component worker<T, R, E> {
    @fate_from(each) reads: queue<T>?
    each: fn(Delivery<T>) -> Result<R, E>
    @fate_for(each) dead: queue<Dead<T, E>>? = null
}
```

The argument `each` is a bare name. It resolves against the component's *own* fields, so the only name involved is the author's own declaration. Precedent (`@bracket("decls")`, `plain_field`) writes it as a string. I'd take whichever the owner prefers; bare is the lead's spelling.

## 2. What the law reads (both paths)

At the declaration, each component field gets a fate seat: `Own` (`@fate`), `For(h)`, `From(h)`, or none.
- Layer: on `FieldSeat` / `RecordShape`, beside the existing `valued`.
- Old path: read off `component_parts_of(d).fields()` marks through `decls.is_meta_annotation`.

An instance of component C owes a fate for handler field `h` only when:
- some field of C is marked `@fate_for(h)` or `@fate_from(h)`; and
- the value written for `h` can fail (a fn answering `Result`).

A component with no marks owes nothing, as one with no `dead` owes nothing today.

The fate is named when **any** of these holds:
- **Direct.** A `@fate_for(h)` field is written non-`null`, or left to a default that is a value (today's `valued` / `defaults_to_value`).
- **Borrowed.** A `@fate_from(h)` field's value traces, through the name (`instance_named` follows the `let` / named instance, as now), to an instance whose `@fate` field is named in the direct sense.
- **Borrowed, untraced.** The value traces to no instance (a parameter, a call's answer). It is taken as named, as now: only a fate known to be missing is refused.

Otherwise the law refuses at `h`'s value, with the same code and message as today. The help names the field **from the mark**, never a constant:
- with only `@fate_for` fields: "name a fate for it — `<field>: …`", where `<field>` is the `@fate_for(h)` field's declared name;
- with a `@fate_from` field: "name the fate on what it reads — `<own field>: …` on `<instance>`", where `<own field>` is the borrowed component's `@fate` field name and `<instance>` is the traced name.

That is the pair's logic unchanged (own first, then queue, then trace through the `let`). Only the key changes: "a field called `dead`" becomes "the field that wears the mark".

## 3. What refuses a mark (new law at the declaration, e.g. `component.fate_mark`; both paths, with witnesses)

1. `@fate_for(h)` or `@fate_from(h)` where `h` names no field of the component: "`h` is no field of `C`".
2. `h` names a field that is not a handler that can fail (not a fn answering `Result`): "a fate is for a handler that can fail; `h` cannot".
3. `@fate_for(h)`, `@fate_from(h)` or `@fate` on a fn-typed field: a handler cannot be a destination.
4. `@fate_from(h)` on a field whose type (with `?` stripped) is not a component declaring a `@fate` field: "`reads` holds a `box`, which marks no `@fate` field to borrow".
5. Two `@fate` fields on one component, or two `@fate_for(h)` fields for the same `h`: ambiguous destination.
6. Any of the three marks outside a component field (a plain record or a fn): refused as misplaced. They mean nothing there.

No field type is required of a direct destination beyond "not a fn". The destination's type is the author's (a `queue<Dead<…>>`, a `Sink`, a `string` name): the compiler doesn't know what a letter is, and that's the point.

## 4. Migration

**std-queue as it stands**
- `worker`: add `@fate_for(each)` on `dead`. That is the only field the law reads today.
- `queue` has **no** `dead` field today, so it has nothing to mark. `@fate_from(each) reads` is added only if and when services move the letter onto the queue: the `queue` then declares `@fate <letter field>`, the `worker` marks `reads`, and the `worker`'s `dead` stays as its own override. Marking `reads` before that refuses under rule 4, deliberately: a borrow from something that has no fate is a mistake.
- `job`: stays unmarked. It always builds its worker with a fate (`buries_in ?? letter_made()`), so it owes nothing at the instance, as today.

**Compiler**
- Delete `fate_field` / `FATE_FIELD`.
- The help strings stop spelling `dead:`, and `fate_unqueued`'s help takes the field names.
- Remedy and witness rows (`remedies.av` around lines 609 and 798, `witnesses.av` around 1453) mark their toy `work` component's `dead`.
- `components_fate_test.av` cases mark their components.
- `tools/program-refusals/fate_*`: the toy `box` gets `@fate dead`, `crew` gets `@fate_from(each) reads` / `@fate_for(each) dead`, and `job` gets `@fate_for(each) dead`. Expectations are unchanged, except that the help names the field from the mark.
- New witnesses: one per refusal in §3, plus a component whose fate field is named something other than `dead` (e.g. `@fate_for(run) graveyard`), to prove nothing keys on the spelling.

**Users.** A user component with a `dead:` field and no mark stops owing a fate. That is a silent loosening, so it needs a note in the release text. Inside the tree the only such components are the toys and std-queue's `worker`, all migrated above.

## Open for the owner
- Bare name or string argument (`@fate_for(each)` vs `@fate_for("each")`).
- Whether `@fate` / `@fate_from` land now (as general machinery, with only the witnesses using them) or with services' move of the letter onto the queue. `@fate_for` alone covers std-queue today.

message.content: Lead: HOLD f49a0160 (the fate pair), and keep it out of your next bundle. services spotted that `flow.no_fate` is keyed on a field literally named `dead` (`const fate_field = "dead"` in features/components/check.av, `FATE_FIELD` in checks.av). That's a queue's vocabulary inside the compiler, and it breaks two rules: no string-matching to detect behavior, and compiler changes must generalize. The general form: a component DECLARES which of its fields is the failure destination for which handler (a mark on the field, e.g. `@fate_for(each)`, a typed `@std/meta` value), and the law reads only marks, naming no field. A queue's `dead:` and a job's are then one user each. Post a design note: the mark's spelling and meaning, how a queue's letter reaches a worker reading it (your traced-through-the-let logic, but keyed by the mark), what refuses a mark on the wrong field type, and the migration for std-queue's current `dead`. Build nothing until I've passed it to services and the owner has seen it.

The re-export recursion is fixed on both paths and amended into 51c10dce; the full gate set is running in the background now. I'll make the `base57..HEAD` bundle once the gates pass.

**What was wrong:** when two modules `export use` each other, following one re-export led straight back to the other, with no end.
- **Old path:** the walk recursed forever, which overflowed the stack in the witnesses test.
- **Layer:** `module_exports` asked for its own answer while it was still working it out.

**What changed:**
- **Old path:** `line_words` now carries a list of modules it has already visited and skips them (`compiler/workspace.av`).
- **Layer:** `module_exports` follows `export use` lines through a plain helper with the same visited list, so the query never asks for itself (`compiler/item_context.av`).
- The idioms complaint is fixed: the lambda in `reexports` now uses `it`.
- New witness `tools/program-refusals/component_reexport_cycle`: two modules that `export use` each other. Both paths print `l r`.

**Checked so far:**
- The witnesses test (`witnesses_test.av`) passes 13/13.
- The witness script holds all 6 re-export and fate cases.
- Gen-2 is byte-for-byte identical to gen-1.

**Found along the way, not chased:** two files in the same directory that each `export use` the other's single-file module get `resolve.duplicate_type` on the layer. The old path runs that case fine. base55 does the same, so it's older than this change. I told the lead.

The only open item before bundling is the gate run.

#   differs.why — the paths are known to differ on it, for the reason written there: it is said
#     and not failed while it differs, and FAILS once it holds, until the file is taken away.
# A case that uses a form only the program layer builds (`avra tapes <case> --new-only`) is never
# asked of the old path, which never learned the form: the program layer alone is held to the
# expectation, and the count of such cases is said.
# Every case is copied to a directory of its own with no store and a machine store of its own, so
# each judgement is cold; a path into that copy is said as `<case>`. Prints each failing case with what differs, then the
# counts; exits 1 on any failure. With PIN=1, a case holding neither expectation is first given
# the old path's: its `check`'s words where it refuses, else what its `run` prints.
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh [compiler] [case…]   (default build/avra-try, every case)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known   (each case known to differ, and why; runs nothing)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --cases   (each case's name, one a line, as the gate deals them)
# A case is a directory holding its `avra.toml` (tools/lib/cases.sh); one that holds none is no case.
# Every case run, each such directory is named; one named on the command line is refused.
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cases_dir="$root/tools/program-refusals"
# the node a wasm case's module runs under: NODE, else /opt/node24's, else the PATH's
node=${NODE:-$( [ -x /opt/node24/bin/node ] && echo /opt/node24/bin/node || echo node )}

. "$root/tools/lib/cases.sh"
# every case, by name
cases() { cases_in "$cases_dir"; }

        return 1
    }
}

held=0
failed=0
if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
    names=""
    for name in "$@"; do
        if [ -f "$cases_dir/$name/avra.toml" ]; then
            names="$names $name"
        else
            echo "$name: no case — tools/program-refusals/$name holds no avra.toml"
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        fi
    done
else
    names=$(cases)
    leftovers_in "$cases_dir" | sed 's/^/witness_program_refusal: leftover /'
fi
known=0
untooled=0
alone=0
for name in $names; do
    why="$cases_dir/$name/differs.why"
    judged "$name" 2>"$tmp/$name.why"

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Bash, Monitor, Read, TaskStop, ToolSearch</tools-used-before-summary>
</system-reminder>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Role and standing setup:**
     - Act as a resumed Avra compiler lane for a controller (the lead), reached through a message bridge.
     - Read `/work/avra/CLAUDE.md` (the project's law) and follow its receipts discipline.
     - Post to the lead inside `<to_controller>...</to_controller>` tags; the claude-bridge tools are absent in this account.
     - Run `[Bridge file transfer]` commands exactly as given.
     - Bundles go to `/work/avra-lane-layer-commands.bundle`, with notes in `/work/avra-lane-layer-commands.md`.
   - **Lead rulings already applied (each listed in Pending Tasks or done):**
     - q6 (C); instance word (A); commas; spread refused with a voice naming `with`; heads by name; a written default is kept; type-argument count refused; fmt gate stays whole.
     - q15, which takes three pieces.
     - Refusals go to stdout, as `check` and the old path do.
     - A Darwin watchdog fix, Darwin only.
     - `flow.no_fate` is this lane's: two repros.
     - Re-exported component words (`/work/asks/reexport_component_use`).
     - After those, the memory work: "5 GB for a suite build is still the largest peak we run, and the program-test phase's ~2 GB is the cheaper half to look at first."
   - **Batch 57 instruction:** merge base57, rebuild gen-2, re-run receipts, and send `base57..HEAD`. Done once as 42717144; later commits add to that bundle.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Paths:** the old path (`AVRA_PROGRAM=0`, TypeCx) and the program layer (`AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0`, Checking, laws reading saved findings). Parity is checked by `tools/witness_program_refusal.sh` over the cases in `tools/program-refusals`:
     - `refuses.expected` / `prints.expected` / `warns.expected`;
     - `differs.why` for a known difference;
     - `PIN=1` pins from the old path.
   - **Gates:**
     - `sh tools/gate.sh <slice> [base]`, driven by my wrapper `/tmp/claude-0/gates.sh`, with `SLICES` set and the fmt/idioms base `a=6abff86d`.
     - Never edit the tree while a gate runs.
     - Container restarts kill background runs; re-run only the lost slices.
   - **Build:**
     - `AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make try`, then `cp build/avra-try build/avra`, then gen-2 compared with `cmp`.
     - Some changes need gen-3 to reach the fixed point.
     - Running fmt with an old `build/avra` can revert new syntax forms.
   - **Laws:**
     - `export law name { kind, reads | reads_view | judge, voice, warns, notes, witness }`.
     - `Seating` enum variants need adding at every registry site (`.StaticUnpinned(_, _) or .Heard(_) ...`) in `compiler/item_refused.av`.
     - Refusal rows `-> Refusal.name` live in a feature's `refusals:`.
     - `avra voices --baseline tools/voices.baseline`; `docs/VOICES.md` is generated by `avra voices --report`.
     - Remedy rows live in `compiler/dev/remedies.av`; witnesses in `compiler/dev/witnesses.av`.
   - **Memory:**
     - `AVRA_MEM_STATS=1`, `AVRA_MEM_SITES=N`, `AVRA_MEM_DUMP_AT=MB`; `addr2line -e build/avra`.
     - The runtime ceiling is per process (mallinfo minus what a fork inherited).
     - `tools/watch.sh` sums PSS on Linux; on Darwin it takes the larger of the RSS sum and the summed footprint.
     - Forks share copy-on-write pages, which RSS and footprint double-count.
   - **Measured facts (avrac-b, gate env, cold):**
     - Summed PSS peak 5.06 GB: the `avra test` parent alone, at t≈781 s.
     - Suite compile reaches 4.05 GB by t≈160 s; the program tests add about 1 GB in t 600–780.
     - The `evaluated_apart` forks copy almost nothing.
     - The lead's 10.1 GB was the Mac watchdog charging each fork the parent's shared pages in full.

3. Files and Code Sections (major edits; all committed):
   - **`tools/watch.sh`** (71e734ea):
     - `rss_sum` reads `pid pgid kb ppid [args…]`; a fork (same args as its in-tree parent) is charged `max(0, mine - parent)`.
     - `tree_rss` on non-Linux uses `ps -eo pid=,pgid=,rss=,ppid=,args=`.
     - `tree_mem` (Darwin) parses `footprint` per-pid headers into KB, joins them with `ps`, and passes them to `rss_sum`.
     - Self-test now has 6 fixtures (forked → 4882 MB, writer → 5906 MB, exec'd → 6835 MB).
   - **Fate pair (a86951ac, amended):**
     - `core/parts.av`: added `fn defaults_to_value(p: Param) -> bool`, `fn instance_named(e: ExprId) -> ExprId?`, `fn bound_as(e: ExprId) -> string?`.
     - `core/checking.av`: `FieldSeat` gains `valued: bool = false`; `Seating.Fateless(word: string, queue: string?)`; `mut fn fateless(handler, word, queue: string?)`.
     - `compiler/item_signatures.av`: sets `valued: item.store.defaults_to_value(f/p)`.
     - `compiler/item_refused.av`:
       - `.Fateless(_, _)` at all 18 sites;
       - `fateless_words` passes `[word].concat(some_list(queue))`;
       - `fateless_refused` chooses `fate_unqueued(a[0], a[1])` when `a.length > 1`.
     - `features/components/checks.av` (layer):
       - `fate_judged` rewritten with helpers `fated`, `lettered`, `queue_fated`;
       - also called for named instances (`if expanded != null { fate_judged(cx, e, instance) }`).
     - `features/components/check.av` (old path):
       - `fate_law(cx, e, x)` with `FateField { declares, valued }` and helpers `fate_of`, `fate_unvalued()`, `record_decl`, `fate_named`, `queue_lettered`;
       - new voice `fate_unqueued(word, queue) = fate_unnamed(word) with { help: "name the letter on the queue it reads — \`dead: <sink>\` on \`${queue}\`" }`.
     - `features/components/semantics.av`: calls `fate_law(cx, e, x)`.
     - Witnesses: `tools/program-refusals/fate_on_queue`, `fate_on_queue_moved`, `fate_job_unset` (prints `own letter`), `fate_letterless_queue`.
   - **Re-export (7943052b):**
     - `compiler/item_context.av` `module_exports`: for each exported `UseLine`, adds `line_shapes(engine, f, u).components` keyed by `c.word`.
     - `compiler/workspace.av`:
       - `line_words` computes `let carried = self.reexported_words(m, u)`, returns `carried` instead of `{}` when the record shortcut finds nothing, and concats `carried.components`;
       - new methods `reexported_words(m, u)` and `exported_lines_words(path)`, which call `line_words` recursively;
       - free fn `reexports(text)`, which lexes for `export` followed by `use`;
       - import `use grammar.{Token, lex_source}`.
     - Witness: `tools/program-refusals/component_reexported_word` (vendor defs + facade with `get` and `get as fetch`; prints `/health ok /ready yes`).
   - Earlier work (q6, instance word A, commas, spread, heads by name, q15 note law, stdout refusals, base56 and base57 merges) is in the bundles and notes.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Fate, idioms duplicated literals:** fixed by `fate_unvalued()` and `fate_unqueued` built from `fate_unnamed`; amended into a86951ac.
   - **Re-export, open (current):**
     - idioms `[closures.pronoun_lambda]` at `(0..ts.length - 1).any((i) -> ts[i].lit_matches("export") && ts[i + 1].lit_matches("use"))`. The fix is to use `it`.
     - avrac-g witnesses test (`compiler/witnesses / the registry, run / every witness that runs produces the code it claims`, `witnesses_test.av:37`) traps with "a task's stack overflowed". Likely cause: unbounded recursion `line_words` → `reexported_words` → `exported_lines_words` → `line_words` over cyclic `export use` among modules. The layer's `module_exports` → `line_shapes` → `module_exports` could likewise hit a query cycle.
   - Earlier fixes (merge conflicts, fmt reverting forms, reserved word `component`, query annotation misplacement, and others) are all resolved.

5. Problem Solving:
   - The memory work established that the real peak is 5.06 GB of summed PSS, and that the Darwin watchdog's double count was fixed in the instrument.
   - The memory investigation was paused: a dump run (`/tmp/claude-0/mem/dump.sh <MB>` with `AVRA_MEM_DUMP_AT`) was stopped for the fate work.
   - A pre-existing parity gap was reported to the lead and not chased: a consumer importing a component the facade does not export gets refusals in a different order, with different parse help, on the two paths.

6. All user messages (summarized; no security constraints beyond these):
   - Initial resume instructions:
     - wait for `HANDOFF.md` and `base55.bundle`;
     - fetch the bundles, check out the branch, build, continue the handoff queue;
     - report in one-line posts; name the branch and file stems `avra-lane-layer-commands`.
   - Bridge file-transfer commands, run as given.
   - The lead rulings and requests listed in section 1, in order:
     - the q6 repro; q6 ruling (C); don't port it to the old path;
     - instance ruling (A); commas; the spread ruling; heads by name;
     - the List default, the type-argument count, and keeping the fmt gate whole;
     - the stdout refusals ask;
     - the batch 56 and batch 57 landing notices;
     - the memory task and its clarifications; the Darwin-only watchdog ruling, with the next memory item;
     - `flow.no_fate` and its two repros;
     - the re-export repro.
   - Several mid-turn messages that arrived empty or as "undefined".

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Fix the re-export recursion with a visited guard on both paths. Old path: a seen-set parameter on `reexported_words` / `exported_lines_words` / `line_words`, or a separate guarded walk. Layer: avoid a query cycle in `module_exports`, for example a non-query helper with a seen-set.
   - Fix the idioms lambda to use `it`.
   - Rebuild to gen-2, re-run the receipts (the re-export and fate witnesses, `witnesses_test`), then the full gate set: fmt, idioms-avrac, idioms, avrac-a through avrac-g, refusal-a/b/c, findings-a through findings-d, doors-a/b, warnings-b, witness-b, cli.
   - Then re-bundle `base57..HEAD` and post it to the lead.
   - Then the memory item: the program-test phase's roughly +1 GB, from 4.05 to 5.06 GB in t 600–780; measure with `AVRA_MEM_DUMP_AT` at the plateau versus the end.
   - The lead runs the Mac half of the watchdog witness.

A component re-exported across packages opens its block where it is imported

A component's word was known by the module that declares it alone, so
one a facade re-exports (`export use @repro.defs.{Route, get}`) left its
word behind: `get "/health" { "ok" }` in the facade's consumer was
`parse.expected`, while the same program importing `@repro/defs` built.
A module's words now carry what its `export use` lines re-export, under
the names they export them as, each word's shape its own module's: the
program layer's `module_exports` reads them through the line's own
shapes, and the old path's `line_words` follows a provider's `export
use` lines before its record answers (a file parsed for them only where
its lexed text writes one). One rule for "this word is a component
here", wherever the name came from.

Witness: tools/program-refusals/component_reexported_word — a facade
re-exporting `get`, and `get as fetch`, from another package; both
instances build and print `/health ok /ready yes` on both paths, and
fail to parse on the compiler before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QBqJupGRwCftk5trAChaRB
EOF

`dead:` field and owed nothing where a component had none, so moving the
letter onto the queue — the owner's surface for services — silently

own fate field, written other than `null` or defaulted to a value
(`FieldSeat.valued`, `defaults_to_value`), else the letter of the queue
a field of it holds — the named instance that name binds
(`instance_named`), fated the same way. Only a fate known missing is
refused, in the queue's words where there is one ("name the letter on
the queue it reads — `dead: <sink>` on `plain`", `fate_unqueued`), the
instance named by the name it binds. A record with no fate field and no
queue owes none, and a queue no name traces is taken as lettered. Both
paths; the program layer now judges a named instance too, which it had
skipped.

declaring `dead:`), fate_on_queue_moved (the owner's shape), fate_job_unset

watch: a fork is charged what it adds, never its parent's pages again

On Darwin the watchdog sums ps's RSS and each process's footprint, and
both charge a forked child every page it still shares with its parent:
the std-avrac suite's `avra test` (~5 GB) and one program test's
evaluating fork read as 10.1 GB, against a real peak Linux's PSS puts
at 5.06 GB — a cost that does not exist, near enough the 12 GB ceiling
to kill a slice. A child running its parent's very command line never
exec'd, so `rss_sum` now charges it only what it holds beyond its
parent; a child that exec'd — another binary, or this one with other
words (`@refuse-eval`) — counts in full, and the spawn-before-exec twin
is counted once as before. The footprint poll goes through the same sum,
each pid's footprint in its RSS's place. Linux keeps summing PSS.

Fixtures (`watch.sh --self-test`, now 6): a fork at its parent's size
charged nothing, a fork that wrote 1 GB of its own charged that GB, an
exec of the same binary counted in full. The Mac half — the slice's
reported peak ≈ Linux's PSS, and a fork that writes a big buffer still
charged — is the lead's to run.

sampler=$!
fi
peak=0
fired=0
# The tree's PHYSICAL FOOTPRINT in MB — `footprint`'s number, which
# counts a page the compressor holds. RSS does not, and read a
# 2.4 GB compiler as 1.4 GB on a machine that then panicked. (tree_mem,
# tree_kill and tree_rss are defined above, ahead of the traps that
# may need to call tree_kill before this point in the file runs.)
# THE STEP IS WAITED FOR, THE TRIPWIRE POLLS BESIDE IT. A warm build is 80 ms of
# work: a loop that looked for its end between polls cost it the poll, and one
# that slept between looks cost it the sleep. The poller keeps the tripwire's
# cadence — RSS every 0.25 s, the footprint every fourth poll, never the first —
# and says what it saw in the lock's own directory, which dies with the step.
state="$lock/watch"
( polls=0; seen=0
  while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
      sleep 0.25
      kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
      rss=$(tree_rss "$pid")
      [ -z "$rss" ] && rss=0
      mem=$rss
      if [ $((polls % 4)) -eq 3 ]; then
          fp=$(tree_mem "$pid")
          [ -n "$fp" ] && [ "$fp" -gt "$mem" ] && mem=$fp
      fi
      polls=$((polls + 1))
      if [ "$mem" -gt "$seen" ]; then seen=$mem; echo "$seen" > "$state.peak"; fi
      if [ "$mem" -gt "$cap_mb" ]; then
          echo 1 > "$state.fired"
          tree_kill "$pid"
          break
      fi
  done ) &
poller=$!
wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
status=$?
kill "$poller" 2>/dev/null
wait "$poller" 2>/dev/null
[ -f "$state.peak" ] && peak=$(cat "$state.peak")
[ -f "$state.fired" ] && fired=1
[ -n "$sampler" ] && wait "$sampler" 2>/dev/null
[ "$fired" -eq 1 ] && status=137
echo "watch: peak ${peak} MB, status ${status}" >&2
exit $status

# THEM: no state, safe wherever a trap needs them, and callable from
# fixture 3 below.
#
# MEMBERSHIP IS BY PROCESS GROUP, NEVER A ppid WALK. A pgid is
# assigned once and never goes stale; a ppid does, the instant a
# parent dies and is reparented away — and once that freed pid is
# reused by an unrelated process elsewhere on a loaded machine, a
# walk matching on ppid attributes the reused pid's whole subtree to
# the wrong root. `tree_pids` takes a `ps -eo pid=,pgid=` snapshot on
# stdin so a hand-built one can prove this by construction.
tree_pids() {
    awk -v root="$1" '$2 == root { print $1 }'
}
tree_mem() {
    pids=$(ps -eo pid=,pgid= | tree_pids "$1")
    [ -n "$AVRA_WATCH_TRACE" ] && footprint $pids 2>/dev/null | awk '/\[[0-9]+\]:.*Footprint:/ { for (i=1; i<=NF; i++) if ($i=="Footprint:") printf "%s %s%s  ", $1, $(i+1), $(i+2) } END { print "" }' >&2
    # a per-process header reads `name [pid]: … Footprint: N MB`; the
    # Summary that follows several pids repeats their total
    footprint $pids 2>/dev/null | awk '
        /\[[0-9]+\]:.*Footprint:/ {
            for (i=1; i<=NF; i++) if ($i=="Footprint:") {
                v=$(i+1)+0; u=$(i+2)
                if (u=="GB") v*=1024; else if (u=="KB") v/=1024; else if (u=="B") v=0
                s+=v
            }
        }
        END { print int(s) }'
}
# WHETHER A SLOT OR A TICKET HAS NO LIVE HOLDER. A holder writes its pid a moment after it
# makes the directory, so a process killed in between (a Sprite's OOM kill) leaves a directory
# with an EMPTY pid, and reading "no pid" as "alive" stalled every later build until someone
# moved it by hand. A dead pid is gone; an empty or missing one is gone once the directory has
# stood a minute, far longer than the moment it is written in.
holder_gone() {
    h=$(cat "$1/pid" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$h" ]; then
        ! kill -0 "$h" 2>/dev/null
        return
    fi
    [ -n "$(find "$1" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +1 2>/dev/null)" ]
}
# Linux only (smaps_rollup); macOS keeps ps's RSS, whose footprint poll is the honest number.
tree_pss() {
    pids=$(ps -eo pid=,pgid= | tree_pids "$1")
    for p in $pids; do echo "/proc/$p/smaps_rollup"; done | xargs cat 2>/dev/null | awk '/^Pss:/ { s += $2 } END { print int(s / 1024) }'
}
tree_rss() {
    if [ -r /proc/self/smaps_rollup ]; then
        tree_pss "$1"
    else
        ps -eo pid=,pgid=,rss=,ppid= | rss_sum "$1"
    fi
}
# THE GUARDED COMMAND BECOMES A PROCESS-GROUP LEADER, WITH OR WITHOUT A
# TTY: its own pgid, equal to its own pid, is what the tree walkers
# above key on — never a ppid chain. `setsid` is preferred, because it
# gives the child a group with no terminal at all; job control is the
# fallback for macOS (no `setsid`), and its stderr is shut because dash
# without a tty answers `set -m` with "can't access tty; job control
# turned off" and leaves it off — a line a caller's output diff reads
# as content, which is how this cost cache-attacks 2/117 on a Sprite.
if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    leader() { setsid "$@" & }
else

The 10.1 GB was the Mac watchdog charging each fork the parent's shared pages in full. That's an instrument reporting a cost that doesn't exist and killing runs for it, so the fix is the instrument, not the program. Restructuring the suite around a measurement artifact would be the wrong move. On Darwin, sum each process's own pages: phys_footprint minus what it shares with its parent, or skip a child whose pages are its parent's, as rss_sum already does for spawn-before-exec. Witness: on the Mac, the same slice's reported peak ≈ Linux's PSS (≈5 GB), and an attack where a fork really writes its pages (it touches a big buffer) is still charged in full. I'll run the Mac half here once it lands. Then your next item: the memory you measured is honest. 5 GB for a suite build is still the largest peak we run, and the program-test phase's ~2 GB is the cheaper half to look at first.

payload.result:
PSS gives the actual answer.
- **Forks add almost nothing.** During the program tests, parent plus fork come to 4.05 GB, the same as the parent alone (2.06 + 2.00 GB, the shared pages split between them). Each fork's own copied memory is under about 10 MB.
- **The real summed peak is 5.06 GB**, the parent alone at the end of the run.

The 9.8–10.1 GB figure is shared pages counted once per process. On Linux, `watch.sh` sums PSS and would report about 5 GB. parity-types' machine paths look like a Mac, where `watch.sh` sums footprints; if that's where the figure came from, footprint is what double-counts the forks.

<to_controller>measured (PSS = each shared page split among its sharers, what watch.sh sums on Linux), `sh tools/gate.sh avrac-b` on 42717144, cold, 1 s samples: summed PSS peaks at 5.06 GB, at t≈781 s, the `avra test` parent alone (end of its program-test phase). During the program tests each `evaluated_apart` fork shows PSS ≈2.0 GB beside the parent's ≈2.06 GB — summing to 4.05 GB, the same as the parent alone (4.05 GB a moment before): the forks copy almost nothing (refcount writes on shared boxes are negligible here). So the 9.8–10.1 GB is the parent's ~5 GB counted twice: RSS (or macOS footprint, which watch.sh sums on Darwin — the land57 run was on a Mac, by its paths) charges each fork the shared pages in full. Two ways to cut what the watchdog sees, need your pick: (1) MEASUREMENT: on Darwin, charge a fork only its own pages (footprint minus what it shares — or, on both, skip a child whose memory is its parent's, as rss_sum already does for spawn-before-exec); (2) STRUCTURE: make the eval legs not forks of a 5 GB parent — run `ran_in` (program tests) BEFORE the suite compile, so the forks come from a parent holding only the program tests' state (~2 GB at that point by my samples), and the suite compile afterwards runs with no fork beside it; the program-test lines print where they do now. (2) cuts the double-counted sum to ≈ max(5.06, ~2+2) — over a third — without touching the watchdog; (1) is honest everywhere but changes a tool other lanes rely on. I lean (2), measured before/after by summed RSS (the double-count proxy) and PSS.</to_controller>

That decision belongs to the lead: fix how the watchdog counts, or change when the forks happen. I'll start once they rule.

By then the parent holds the whole suite compile's state (about 4.9 GB). The child walks the lowered program, writes refcounts as it goes, and so copies every page it touches.

- Release the suite compile's state before the program tests run.
- Have the eval leg start from a small process that loads only the one lowered program.

I'll measure summed PSS first (the "before" figure), once the gate run frees the machine.

#!/bin/sh
# tool-witness: --self-test
# A BOUNDED STEP NAMES ITS CAUSE. The command runs under `timeout` (and a
# kill ten seconds after), answers its own status, and on failure says which
# of three it was: past its bound (124), killed (137: a memory cap or the
# bound's kill), or a failure with its exit code. Under GitHub Actions the
# words are an `::error::` annotation.
#
#   sh tools/bounded.sh <seconds> <command> [args...]
#   sh tools/bounded.sh --self-test

said() {
    rc=$1 secs=$2; shift 2
    case $rc in
        124) why="ran past its $secs s bound" ;;
        137) why="was killed (exit 137: a memory cap or the bound's kill; see the peak line)" ;;
        *) why="failed (exit $rc)" ;;
    esac
    echo "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:+::error::}\`$*\` $why"
}

bounded() {
    secs=$1; shift
    timeout -k 10 "$secs" "$@"
    rc=$?
    [ "$rc" = 0 ] || said "$rc" "$secs" "$@"
    return "$rc"
}

self_test() {
    fails=0
    bad() { fails=$((fails + 1)); echo "bounded: FAIL — $1"; }
    out=$(bounded 5 true) || bad "a passing command failed"
    [ -z "$out" ] || bad "a passing command spoke: $out"
    out=$(bounded 5 sh -c 'exit 3'); rc=$?
    [ "$rc" = 3 ] || bad "a failure answered $rc, not its own 3"
    case "$out" in *"failed (exit 3)"*) ;; *) bad "a failure said: $out" ;; esac
    out=$(bounded 1 sleep 5); rc=$?
    [ "$rc" = 124 ] || bad "a command past its bound answered $rc, not 124"
    case "$out" in *"ran past its 1 s bound"*) ;; *) bad "a command past its bound said: $out" ;; esac
    out=$(GITHUB_ACTIONS=true bounded 5 false)
    case "$out" in "::error::"*) ;; *) bad "under Actions the words are no annotation: $out" ;; esac
    [ "$fails" = 0 ] || exit 1
    echo "bounded: self-test passed — 4 fixtures (silent pass, own status, the bound, the annotation)"
}

case "$1" in
    --self-test) self_test ;;
    ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "usage: sh tools/bounded.sh <seconds> <command> [args...] | --self-test" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *) bounded "$@" ;;
esac

I can't reproduce the 10.1 GB peak in a single process yet, so I haven't cut anything. Run exactly as the gate runs it (`sh tools/gate.sh avrac-b`, cold), the largest single process is about 5.1 GB, on both my branch and the base57 merge.

Two moments add up high, but only if you sum every process's resident memory:
- **The slice's own compiler build**, which runs first when HEAD's compiler isn't already built: a parent plus four worker forks, 12.8 GB summed.
- **The end of the suite compile**: the 4.9 GB parent plus a fork of it at 4.9 GB, 9.8 GB summed. This is the closest match to the reported figure.

Both sums count memory a fork still shares with its parent, so the real total is lower. The runtime's 12 GB ceiling is checked per process and charges a fork only for what it adds, so neither sum would trip it.

My first measurements also had the net on, a mode the gate turns off. That mode does produce one 9.8 GB process, which is where my early 10 GB match came from.

I've asked the lead how the 10,147,008 kB was measured and on which tree: per process on Linux, or a summed, container-level or Sprite figure. Whichever process owns that number is the one to cut, and the 1.85 GB of untracked bytes in the suite-compile parent remains the first suspect.

Batch 57 is merged into the branch (42717144). Another lane fixed the same named-argument bug in base57, so I kept their fix, dropped mine, and my repro still passes on theirs. The compiler builds itself to the same binary on the third build, and all my receipts still hold. The full gate run for the `base57..HEAD` bundle is in progress.

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS BUILD: exact retain/release/list-write counts, and the
# callers that cause them. Counting costs ~8% of a run, so it never
# ships: a census compiler is built BESIDE build/avra, from a runtime
# compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, and the shipping runtime library is
# rebuilt on every exit.
#   sh tools/census.sh check packages/std-avrac
#
# THE SHIPPING COMPILER IS NEVER REMOVED. It builds the census
# compiler, so a census that deletes it first has nothing to build
# with, and every recovery that rebuilds needs the memory and disk the
# census run just spent.
#
# CENSUS_EDIT MEASURES A WARM EDIT: the command runs once cold to fill the store,
# then CENSUS_EDIT edits the tree, and only the run after it is counted.
#   CENSUS_EDIT='sh tools/db_measure/edit_literal.sh' sh tools/census.sh check packages/cli
#
# A CENSUS THAT PRINTS NO COUNTS FAILS. A check that examined nothing
# is not a check that passed: no `rc:` line means the binary carried no
# census, and the run exits 1 saying so.
# A cold run clears the tree's `.avra-cache`; the machine store lives there too, or "cold" would read the machine's rows.
export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.avra-cache"
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
: "${LLVM_PREFIX:=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm}"
export LLVM_PREFIX

# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK, under a memory cap: the old path's check the net runs
# before the program layer's is not that work, and its memory with the layer's passes the cap.
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
census=build/avra.census
stores=.avra-cache.census-saved
suffix=.census-saved
named="$*"
restore() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
    if [ -d "$stores" ]; then rm -rf .avra-cache; mv "$stores" .avra-cache; fi
    for d in $named; do
        if [ -d "$d/.avra-cache$suffix" ]; then rm -rf "$d/.avra-cache"; mv "$d/.avra-cache$suffix" "$d/.avra-cache"; fi
    done
}
trap restore EXIT INT TERM

rm -rf "$stores"
[ -d .avra-cache ] && mv .avra-cache "$stores"
sh tools/census_compiler.sh "$census"

# THE MEASURED RUN STARTS COLD: the census compiler's store is its own
# and was never filled, and the tree's stores stand aside until exit.
# THE FILTER DROPS `mem:`, IT DOES NOT SELECT LABELS: an allowlist of
# census labels is a second registry of them, and goes stale silently.
# A PACKAGE NAMED ON THE COMMAND KEEPS ITS OWN STORE (`tapes <pkg>` writes `<pkg>/.avra-cache`), so it
# stands aside too, or the second census of one package reads the first one's answers.
rm -rf .avra-cache
for d in "$@"; do
    if [ -d "$d/.avra-cache" ]; then rm -rf "$d/.avra-cache$suffix"; mv "$d/.avra-cache" "$d/.avra-cache$suffix"; fi
done
if [ -n "${CENSUS_EDIT:-}" ]; then
    sh tools/memcap.sh "${CENSUS_CAP_MB:-4000}" "$census" "$@" > build/census-cold.out 2>&1 || { tail -5 build/census-cold.out; echo "census: the cold run failed"; exit 1; }
    sh -c "$CENSUS_EDIT"
fi
out="$(AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_CENSUS_SITES=1 sh tools/memcap.sh "${CENSUS_CAP_MB:-4000}" "$census" "$@" 2>&1 >/dev/null \
    | tee build/census-raw.out | grep -Ev '^(mem:|memcap:)' || true)"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^rc:' || { printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -5; echo "census: the run printed no counts"; exit 1; }

An instance of a template whose event is refused notes it, pointing where it is declared

A template declares no event, and an instance of one is not built: the
old path said a note at each instance pointing at the refused event, and
the program layer now does too (`template_instance_noted`, its voice
`event_refused_there` shared with the old path), wherever the template
is declared — the instance's word resolves through the file's words to
the component and the file declaring it.

What that took, each its own piece:
- A law may NOTE (`law.notes`): its finding is a note beside a refusal
  another law says, and a law speaks at one severity, so `check()`
  refuses one that both warns and notes.
- An aside may stand in another file (`Aside.file`, `AsideAt.file`), its
  place counted from that file's start; a `ProgramFile` names any file
  as its run does (`named`), and `finding_diag` takes the file it says,
  so the frame names the right path.
- A report says each file holding a refusal before the files holding
  only the notes that point at one (`refusals_first`, for `build`/`run`
  and the test harness; `check` orders its files so too, renders each
  diagnostic over every file its frames name, and parts files by a
  blank line as the other reports do).

An instance fills its heads by name, keeps an unset field's default, and counts its type arguments

Three rules an instance holds now that a component's name before a

- A head is a field, so the block may fill it by name, as a record
  literal's spelling does: `pair { a: 1, b: 2 }`, `pair 1 { b: 2 }`. A
  head is filled once — written as a head value, or named in the block,
  never both (refused, naming it) — and every head one way or the other
  ("`pair` needs `a` and `b`: write them as head values or name them in
  the block"). The two std sites that built a component with two heads,

  unset field takes its default: `ChildSlot.defaulted` says the field
  writes one, so only a slot with none is filled empty.

  judge the literal an instance builds.

#!/bin/sh
# A PACKAGE'S SUITE ON THE PROGRAM LAYER SAYS WHAT THE OLD RUNNER SAYS, AND AN EDIT OF ONE CASE
# WORKS OUT THAT CASE ALONE. tools/program-suites/suited holds a spec whose cases pass but one,
# which is wrong on purpose, a lone case in no group, a program test and a test run as a child:
#   `avra test` of it on the old path and on the program layer (each cold) — the same exit, the same
#     stdout byte for byte, the failing case's sides and the runner's verdict included;
#   then, on the program layer, one `then` body edited and the suite tested warm: exactly one case
#     lowered again, and the same stdout as the edited tree tested cold.
#   sh tools/witness_program_suites.sh [compiler]   (default build/avra-try)
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
avra=${1:-build/avra-try}
case $avra in /*) ;; *) avra="$root/$avra" ;; esac
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "witness_program_suites: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'find "$tmp" -delete' EXIT
failed=0
missed() { echo "witness_program_suites: $1" >&2; failed=$((failed + 1)); }

# `avra test suited` under AVRA_PROGRAM=$1 in the copy $2 — a fresh one with no store, `edited.av`
# standing as the edited file where $3 is `edited`, or the copy as it stands where $3 is `warm`: its
# stdout said with the copy's path as <w>, its exit, its stderr
tested() {
    if [ "${3:-}" != warm ]; then
        find "$tmp/$2" "$tmp/$2.machine" -depth -delete 2>/dev/null
        mkdir -p "$tmp/$2" "$tmp/$2.machine"
        cp -R "$root/tools/program-suites/suited" "$tmp/$2/"
        [ "${3:-}" = edited ] && cp "$tmp/edited.av" "$tmp/$2/$edited"
program-suites
suites_links.sh
witness_program_suites.sh
witness_two_suites.sh

#!/bin/sh
# THE CHANGED-FILE FMT CHECK — ONE definition, called by the gate's own fmt
# step (.github/workflows/checks.yml) and by `tools/work land`'s local
# preflight, so the two can never drift into two instruments.
#
#   sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head>     # the caller has refs (the gate)
#   sh tools/fmt_changed.sh --files <files…>  # the caller already diffed
#
# Every named `.av` file is run through `fmt --check`. The compiler is
# `${AVRA:-build/avra}` — the tree under test's OWN build. THE BRANCH'S
# COMPILER, NEVER A STALE STANDING ONE: a binary that predates the syntax a
# branch added REFUSES that branch's files and cannot report the canonical
# diff, so it would certify a file the gate then refuses. The gate has its
# own build; a lane's Sprite holds a branch build (`tools/work run`), and its
# synced tree carries no `.git`, which is why `--files` exists. Nothing
# here polls `main`: the refs are named, never watched.
set -eu
[ "$#" -ge 1 ] || { echo "fmt_changed: usage: sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head> | --files <files…>" >&2; exit 2; }
avra=${AVRA:-build/avra}
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "fmt_changed: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 2; }
if [ "$1" = --files ]; then
    shift
    changed=$*
else
    [ "$#" -eq 2 ] || { echo "fmt_changed: usage: sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head>" >&2; exit 2; }
    changed=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d "$1" "$2" -- '*.av')
fi
[ -n "$changed" ] || { echo "fmt_changed: no changed .av to check"; exit 0; }
"$avra" fmt --check $changed

use @std.grammar.{Grammar, Rule, Alt, Seq, Item, Prim, Rep, Build, Expect, Recover}
use diagnostics.{DiagCode}

export fn components() -> LanguageFeature {
    let codes = table<DiagCode> {
        kind                      | summary
        "type.component_expand"   | "a component's `expand` answers the code an instance becomes"
        "type.component_twice"    | "a template reads each of its instance's fields once"
        "type.component_check"    | "a component's `check` answers `List<Diagnostic>`"
        "lower.component_checked" | "a component's `check` judged this instance"
        "type.component_format"   | "a `Format` head is `@std.meta`'s pattern type"
        "type.component_event"    | "an instance hears the events its component declares"
        "type.component_body"     | "a component's body is what one trait says a body is"
        "type.component_head"     | "the brace after an instance's head opens the instance's block"
        "type.component_row"      | "a repeated row that keeps state wears a key"
        "type.component_default"  | "a member's default reads only its component's plain inputs"
        "type.slot_shadows"       | "an instance's block names its component's slot before a component of that name"
        "flow.no_fate"            | "a handler that can fail must name a fate for its failure"
    }
    LanguageFeature components {
        gram: grammar {
            stmt = "component" name:NAME ( "<" tparams:tparam ( "," tparams:tparam )* ","? ">" )? ( "(" ( head:hseat ( "," head:hseat )* ","? )? ")" )? "{" ( members:cfield | members:cevent | ".." ( third:"." )? spreads:type | body:stmt | BREAK )* "}" END @recover(sync_to: "END") -> Stmt.ComponentDecl by component_decl_written
            hseat = ( marks:mark )* ( state_field:STATE )? name:NAME ":" ty:type -> Record.ParamSyntax
            cfield = ( marks:mark )* ( state_field:STATE )? name:NAME ":" ty:type ( "=" default:expression )? -> Record.ParamSyntax

That rules out a pure `( "," x )*` list: the members of an instance block are statements, and each statement ends with its own `END`. message.content: Lead ruling on commas: accept them. An instance block's settings take an optional `,` between them, and a trailing one, exactly as a record literal's fields do; a line break still separates without one. One-line instances (`tray { capacity: 0, label: "x" }`) are what a writer reaches for, and P1 says refusing them is a trap, not a style. Do it as its own commit, in the grammar's comma-list shape: `( "," x )*` ends `","?` before its closer. Witness: imported and own-module instances, one-line with commas, multi-line without, and a trailing comma, all on both paths. Then /work/asks/named.

A check builds only what it reads, and says when it cannot run

An instance's `check` runs over its receiver built of what the
component's members read off `self`: a defaulted field no member reads
is left unbuilt (`fields_unread`, `Lowering.unbuilt_field`), so a
default only a run can make no longer keeps a check from judging an
instance. A member handing `self` on whole reads every field.

A check that still reaches what only a run makes warns once at the
instance, in one voice for both paths (`check_unreached`, law
`instance_check_unreached`), naming what it reaches as a reader spells
it. Silence was the old answer; the instance is fine and the check is
unproven, so it warns rather than refuses.

`self.name` reads are one verb on the store (`self_read_at`), and
`names_off_self` answers what a set of nodes reads, absent where `self`
escapes.

default only a run can build" — a check that never reads such a default
refuses, one that builds it warns, one that hands `self` on whole warns.

# whether the case `$1` holds; what differs said on stderr where it doesn't
judged() {
    name=$1
    from="$cases_dir/$name"
    cp -R "$from" "$tmp/$name"
    find "$tmp/$name" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \;
    mkdir -p "$tmp/$name.machine"
    export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$tmp/$name.machine"
    target=$(cat "$from/target" 2>/dev/null || true)
    forms=$(AVRA_PROGRAM=1 "$avra" tapes "$tmp/$name" --new-only 2>/dev/null)
    [ -z "$forms" ] || { judged_alone "$name"; return $?; }
    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
        (cd "$tmp/$name" && AVRA_PROGRAM=0 "$avra" build --target "$target" . >"$tmp/$name.old" 2>&1)
    else
        (cd "$tmp/$name" && AVRA_PROGRAM=0 "$avra" check . >"$tmp/$name.old" 2>&1)
    fi
    old=$?
    (cd "$tmp/$name" && AVRA_PROGRAM=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 "$avra" build ${target:+--target "$target"} . >"$tmp/$name.new" 2>&1)
    new=$?
    said "$name" old >"$tmp/$name.old.said"
    said "$name" new >"$tmp/$name.new.said"
    if [ -n "$target" ] && [ "$old" = 2 ] && [ "$new" = 2 ] && cmp -s "$tmp/$name.old.said" "$tmp/$name.new.said"; then
        return 2
    fi
    if [ "${PIN:-}" = 1 ] && [ ! -e "$from/refuses.expected" ] && [ ! -e "$from/prints.expected" ]; then
        if [ "$old" = 1 ]; then
            cp "$tmp/$name.old.said" "$from/refuses.expected"
        else
            if [ -n "$target" ]; then
                (cd "$tmp/$name" && AVRA_PROGRAM=0 "$avra" build --target "$target" . >/dev/null 2>&1 && "$node" --no-warnings "$root/tools/run_wasm.mjs" src/main.wasm >"$from/prints.expected" 2>/dev/null)
            else
                (cd "$tmp/$name" && AVRA_PROGRAM=0 "$avra" run . >"$from/prints.expected" 2>/dev/null)
            fi
        fi
    fi
    if [ -e "$from/warns.expected" ]; then
        for path in old new; do
            grep '^warning\[' "$tmp/$name.$path" | cmp -s - "$from/warns.expected" || {
                echo "$name: the $path path's warnings differ from warns.expected" >&2
                grep '^warning\[' "$tmp/$name.$path" | diff "$from/warns.expected" - >&2
                return 1
            }
        done
    fi
    if [ -e "$from/refuses.expected" ]; then
        [ "$old" = 1 ] || { echo "$name: the old path's check exited $old, not 1" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.old.said" >&2; return 1; }
        [ "$new" = 1 ] || { echo "$name: the program layer's build exited $new, not 1" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.new.said" >&2; return 1; }
        cmp -s "$tmp/$name.old.said" "$from/refuses.expected" || {
            echo "$name: the old path's words differ from refuses.expected" >&2
            diff "$from/refuses.expected" "$tmp/$name.old.said" >&2
            return 1
        }
        cmp -s "$tmp/$name.new.said" "$from/refuses.expected" || {
            echo "$name: the program layer's words differ from refuses.expected" >&2
            diff "$from/refuses.expected" "$tmp/$name.new.said" >&2
            return 1
        }
        return 0
    fi
    [ "$old" = 0 ] || { echo "$name: the old path's check refused it ($old)" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.old.said" >&2; return 1; }
    [ "$new" = 0 ] || { echo "$name: the program layer refused it ($new)" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.new.said" >&2; return 1; }
    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
        (cd "$tmp/$name" && "$node" --no-warnings "$root/tools/run_wasm.mjs" src/main.wasm) >"$tmp/$name.ran" 2>&1 || { echo "$name: its module failed" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.ran" >&2; return 1; }
    else
        "$tmp/$name/src/main" >"$tmp/$name.ran" 2>&1 || { echo "$name: its product failed" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.ran" >&2; return 1; }
    fi
    cmp -s "$tmp/$name.ran" "$from/prints.expected" || {
        echo "$name: its product printed otherwise" >&2
        diff "$from/prints.expected" "$tmp/$name.ran" >&2
        return 1
    }
}

held=0
failed=0
if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
    names=""
    for name in "$@"; do
        if [ -f "$cases_dir/$name/avra.toml" ]; then
            names="$names $name"
        else
            echo "$name: no case — tools/program-refusals/$name holds no avra.toml"
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        fi
    done
else
    names=$(cases)
    leftovers_in "$cases_dir" | sed 's/^/witness_program_refusal: leftover /'
fi
known=0
untooled=0
alone=0
for name in $names; do
    why="$cases_dir/$name/differs.why"
    judged "$name" 2>"$tmp/$name.why"
    judgement=$?
    if [ "$judgement" = 3 ]; then
        held=$((held + 1))
        alone=$((alone + 1))
    elif [ "$judgement" = 2 ]; then
        echo "$name: untooled — no toolchain here for $(cat "$cases_dir/$name/target"); both paths refuse alike"
        untooled=$((untooled + 1))
    elif [ "$judgement" = 0 ]; then
        if [ -e "$why" ]; then
            echo "$name: holds now, yet differs.why says the paths differ — take the file away"
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        else
            held=$((held + 1))
        fi
    elif [ -e "$why" ]; then
        echo "$name: known to differ — $(head -1 "$why")"
        known=$((known + 1))
    else
        cat "$tmp/$name.why"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
    fi
done
echo "witness_program_refusal: $held of $((held + failed + known)) cases hold, $known known to differ, $failed failing$([ "$untooled" = 0 ] || echo ", $untooled untooled"); $alone skipped by the old path (a form only the program layer builds), held on the program layer alone"
[ "$failed" = 0 ]

#!/bin/sh
# THE GATE, IN SLICES: every receipt a landing is held to, cut into slices that each run alone in a
# tree of their own, so N machines run N slices at once and the gate takes as long as its longest
# slice. A slice builds the compiler of HEAD itself when build/avra was built from anything else,
# runs every row on the program layer, the net off but where a row's claim is the net, empties the
# stores a cold row reads, bounds every command, keeps each row's words under build/gate/<slice>/, and
# ends with ONE line:
#   GATE <slice> <sha8> PASS|FAIL rows=<n> failed=<n> <seconds>s
# exiting 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
#
#   sh tools/gate.sh list               each slice, one a line, with what it holds
#   sh tools/gate.sh <slice> [arg]      one slice; the idioms slices take the base sha their diff starts at
#   sh tools/gate.sh seed               build/gate/compiler-<sha8>.tar.gz: HEAD's compiler — ONE generation, built
#                                       here first where none of HEAD's stands — and every object a tree
#                                       links with; `pack` is its other name. Run it once; every slice
#                                       then starts from `unpack` and builds nothing.
#   sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>      seeds this tree from a pack, and holds its stamp to HEAD's: a
#                                       seeded slice builds no compiler
#
# A test row runs every suite (AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1), so it names every failing case, never only the first.
#
# GATE_OLD_PATH=0 drops every row that compares against the old path (they read AVRA_PROGRAM=0);
# when the old path goes, its default goes to 0 and those rows go with one line each.
# THE NET IS OFF unless a row's claim is the net: the old path's check before every program-layer
# compile doubles what each row costs and proves nothing a row here asks of it. The rows that keep it
# (AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1) are the ones that count what it says: the build slice's net-on cli builds and
# their "program-layer false refusal" count, the findings slices' build of every package, held to that
# same count, and the cli's suite, which holds the words a user meets through a child build/avra (at
# slice_cli). `tapes --findings` passes no door, so the net never stood in it.
# the bound of one row, and of a compiler build
# every `test` row's failing NAMES are held to tools/gate/<package>.names, the cases a sandbox fails
# the packages whose tests the doors slices run

#!/bin/sh
# THE PROGRAM LAYER REFUSES WHAT THE OLD PATH REFUSES, IN ITS WORDS, AND BUILDS WHAT IT BUILDS.
# Each case under tools/program-refusals/ is a package of its own:
#   refuses.expected — the source must be refused: the old path's `check` and the program
#     layer's `build` each exit 1, and what each says, its warnings aside, is exactly this text;
#   prints.expected — the source must not be refused: the old path's `check` exits 0, the
#     program layer builds it, and what the product prints is exactly this text;
#   target — a case for another target, its triple: each path BUILDS it for that target, the build's
#     refusal is its words, and a printing case's module runs under node (`tools/run_wasm.mjs`); on a
#     machine with no toolchain for the target, both paths refuse in the toolchain's same words, exit 2,
#     and the case is said untooled, neither held nor failed;
#   warns.expected — beside either: each path's warnings, their first lines in the order said, are
#     exactly this text (for a case only the program layer builds, that layer's warnings); an
#     empty one says no warning is said;
#   differs.why — the paths are known to differ on it, for the reason written there: it is said
#     and not failed while it differs, and FAILS once it holds, until the file is taken away.
# A case that uses a form only the program layer builds (`avra tapes <case> --new-only`) is never
# asked of the old path, which never learned the form: the program layer alone is held to the
# expectation, and the count of such cases is said.
# Every case is copied to a directory of its own with no store and a machine store of its own, so
# each judgement is cold; a path into that copy is said as `<case>`. Prints each failing case with what differs, then the
# counts; exits 1 on any failure. With PIN=1, a case holding neither expectation is first given
# the old path's: its `check`'s words where it refuses, else what its `run` prints.
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh [compiler] [case…]   (default build/avra-try, every case)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known   (each case known to differ, and why; runs nothing)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --cases   (each case's name, one a line, as the gate deals them)
# A case is a directory holding its `avra.toml` (tools/lib/cases.sh); one that holds none is no case.
# Every case run, each such directory is named; one named on the command line is refused.
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cases_dir="$root/tools/program-refusals"
# the node a wasm case's module runs under: NODE, else /opt/node24's, else the PATH's
node=${NODE:-$( [ -x /opt/node24/bin/node ] && echo /opt/node24/bin/node || echo node )}

. "$root/tools/lib/cases.sh"
# every case, by name
cases() { cases_in "$cases_dir"; }

if [ "${1:-}" = --cases ]; then
    cases
    exit 0
fi

if [ "${1:-}" = --known ]; then
    n=0
    for name in $(cases); do
        [ -e "$cases_dir/$name/differs.why" ] || continue
        echo "$name: $(head -1 "$cases_dir/$name/differs.why")"
        n=$((n + 1))
    done
    echo "witness_program_refusal: $n of $(cases | wc -l | tr -d ' ') cases known to differ"
    exit 0
fi
avra=${1:-build/avra-try}
case $avra in /*) ;; *) avra="$root/$avra" ;; esac
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "witness_program_refusal: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
